newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil may export two million tonnes corn in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Brazil may export two million tonnes corn in 1997.

text.p: Brazil could export up to two million tonnes corn in 1997 given attractive world prices and the recent removal of a state export tax, said the head of the cotton and corn committee at the Sao Paulo bourse.

"I believe that the amount we export should become quite significant even if we import some corn later in the year between crops," said Carlos Murilo Pereira de Mello who is also director of commodities at Cotia Trading.
Brazil has already this year exported around 300,000 to 400,000 tonnes in the May to July period when the harvest coincided with good international prices, de Mello said.

Wth the lifting of the export tax in mid-September this year, this should grow to one million to two million tonnes in 1997 and eventually Brazil could be selling around five million tonnes to customers in Africa and Latin America, he added.

"With the state export tax at 13 percent, it was impossible given the cost of production in Brazil to export. Now however with the tax gone and better international prices, it is a different scenario," de Mello said.
Corn production in 1996/97 de Mello estimates at 33.5 million to 34 million tonnes against a 1995/96 drought-hit harvest of around 30.5 million tonnes.
Even if Brazil stepped up exports, it would still probably continue to import some corn for logistical reasons.
This is particularly true in the north of the country where it is easier and cheaper to buy corn from the U.S. than to transport Brazilian corn from the key southern producing regions, he added.
-- Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151
